items.title: Fatal drowning reported near Tallebudgera Creek
items.summary: ABC Gold Coast reports a man died near Tallebudgera Creek on 23 November.
items.body: ABC Gold Coast reported on 24 November that a 41-year-old visitor died after being pulled unconscious from the water near Tallebudgera Creek the previous day. Police said the death was not suspicious and will prepare a report for the coroner. Follow lifeguard advice and swim only in designated patrolled areas. This report is not a shark alert or beach closure.

items.title: New study links bull shark coastal occurrence to warmer water and rainfall
items.summary: University of the Sunshine Coast-led research analyses 27 years of Queensland shark records.
items.body: A university research release published on 24 November describes associations between coastal bull shark records and water temperature, rainfall and other ocean conditions. The study covers Queensland waters from the Gold Coast to Cairns and reports regional and seasonal differences, with larger sharks more frequently caught in summer and autumn. These are historical catch-data associations, not a prediction of shark presence at any particular beach today. Follow official beach safety advice. Scientific paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fishres.2026.107882.
items.source_name: University of the Sunshine Coast via Phys.org

items.title: Police step up public safety presence for Schoolies in Surfers Paradise
items.summary: Queensland Government announces targeted police operations during Schoolies celebrations.
items.body: A Queensland Government statement on 22 November confirms additional public safety activity in the Surfers Paradise entertainment precinct during Schoolies. Police said officers would remain visible throughout the celebrations and engage with school leavers. This is a precinct safety update, not a beach closure.

items.title: Gold Coast unveils draft designs for Mermaid Beach North Oceanway
items.summary: Council unveils draft designs for an 850-metre coastal shared pathway from Pratten Park to Ocean Street.
items.body: In its 18 November 2026 media release, City of Gold Coast unveiled draft designs for the Mermaid Beach North Oceanway, a proposed 850-metre, five-metre-wide shared pathway connecting Pratten Park in Broadbeach to Ocean Street in Mermaid Beach. The planned works include up to 100 metres of seawall reconstruction and dune planting. Council states construction is expected to begin mid-2027, subject to the project process. This is a planning announcement, not a current access closure.

items.title: The Spit South beach access closed due to erosion
items.summary: City of Gold Coast lists The Spit South beach as closed until further notice due to severe erosion and unstable sand scarps.
items.body: The City of Gold Coast's official The Spit South beach page states that severe erosion and sand scarps linked to Tropical Cyclone Alfred and seasonal high tides have affected access. The beach is listed as closed until further notice. This is an erosion-related closure, not a shark alert; check the council page before visiting.

items.title: Gold Coast endorses proposed night surfing trial at Snapper Rocks
items.summary: Council backs temporary lighting trial for the 2027 world surfing event; permits are still required.
items.body: The Guardian reported on 11 November that council endorsed a temporary lighting trial at Snapper Rocks. The proposal remains subject to permits; environmental and shark-risk concerns have been raised.

items.title: The Spit North beach access remains closed due to erosion
items.summary: City of Gold Coast lists The Spit North beach as closed until further notice due to erosion and unstable sand scarps.
items.body: The official City of Gold Coast beach information page reports The Spit North closed until further notice after severe erosion and sand scarps associated with Tropical Cyclone Alfred and seasonal high tides. This is an erosion-related beach access closure, not a shark alert. Check council notices before visiting.

items.locality: Miami / Mermaid Beach / Surfers Paradise / Main Beach
items.title: Gold Coast reports 1.2 million cubic metres of sand restored to beaches
items.summary: City reports major 2026 offshore dredging works replenished beaches from Miami to Main Beach.
items.body: In an 8 October 2026 update, City of Gold Coast said offshore dredging between April and October had returned approximately 1.2 million cubic metres of sand to Gold Coast beaches, including Miami, Mermaid Beach, Surfers Paradise and Main Beach. The work was part of recovery and beach nourishment efforts following Tropical Cyclone Alfred.

shark_alerts.title: Multiple sharks sighted near swimmers at Greenmount
shark_alerts.detail: Greenmount Beach was closed twice after up to five sharks were sighted near swimmers. This is the latest verified notification currently stored for Greenmount Beach; it is historical, not a current beach closure.
shark_alerts.source_name: Courier Mail / Gold Coast shark sighting report

shark_alerts.title: Surfer knocked from board by shark at Cabarita
shark_alerts.detail: Matthew Devine was knocked from his board by a shark at Cabarita Beach around 4pm and returned to shore without a shark-bite injury. He suspected a bull shark, but the species was not confirmed. This is the latest verified notification currently stored for Cabarita Beach; it is historical, not a current alert.

shark_alerts.title: Tagged bull shark detected at Clarkes Beach
shark_alerts.detail: Tagged bull shark #3362 was detected by the Clarkes Beach, Byron Bay listening station at 3:03:12am AEDT on 31 October 2026. The timestamp is stored here in Australia/Brisbane time. This is a historical tagged-shark detection, not a current beach closure.
